verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input is a company press release and the central inference was published two days after the filing. The Block ran the production decline as wire copy on the filing date itself (2026-08-17, 'Bitcoin production slips again in July for CleanSpark, BitFuFu and Canaan', naming Canaan as the worst of the three at -28% to 46 BTC), and CryptoSlate on 2026-08-19 drew out precisely the hunter's core point in its headline -- that the paused Ethiopia 4.96 EH/s is ~35% of the 14.24 EH/s July 'operating' total -- and even made the June 0.36 vs July 4.96 comparison the hunter treats as the discovery. The filing verifies out (I confirmed 46 BTC, Ethiopia 4.96/4.96 with 'Canaan has paused its mining operations in Ethiopia, but its hashrate remains part of the Company's installed hashrate'), and it is in fact WORSE than stated: group operating power was 7.45 EH/s in the June release and 14.24 EH/s in the July one, so the whole operating column appears to have been backfilled with installed values. But the residual novelty is arithmetic on published monthlies, not a new fact. And the reach into a 30-June print is limited: Q2 self-mined output (90 April + 90 May + 64 June = 244 BTC) was pre-disclosed month by month, so the mining revenue line is effectively already public; the 46-BTC July collapse and any Ethiopia impairment land in Q3, and the June outage began only 'in mid-June' per the company. The -0.43% reaction on 2026-08-17 is a market that read the release and shrugged.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Wire coverage on the filing date: Canaan's July output fell ~28% to 46 BTC from 64 BTC, the biggest decline of the three miners and a second consecutive monthly drop.

Headline article stating Canaan counted the paused Ethiopia 4.96 EH/s inside its 14.24 EH/s July operating hashrate -- nearly 35% of the total -- and contrasting it with June's 0.36 EH/s operating against 4.96 EH/s installed.

June update: 64 BTC, group operating 7.45 EH/s vs installed 14.86, Ethiopia 0.36/4.96, attributed to 'one mining site being temporarily taken offline beginning in mid-June due to local power grid maintenance'.

May update: 90 BTC self-mined plus 24 BTC from customer payments, group operating 9.29 EH/s, Ethiopia 2.20/4.96 -- so operating was already well below installed a month before the hunter's inflection.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2026-08-17 6-K printed -0.43%, and the 2026-07-14 June update (the release that first showed Ethiopia at 0.36 EH/s) printed +0.69%. Both non-events. The +68.2% 20-day run is dated to macro, not to operations: the stock closed $0.2712 on 2026-08-20 after +12.95% on the CLARITY Act push and then +16% on 2026-08-25 into Bitcoin Asia. The tape has been trading crypto beta straight through this operational deterioration, which cuts both ways -- it argues the market has not marked the deterioration, but also that it does not intend to.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the Q2 balance sheet takes an Ethiopia-specific impairment or that management guides Q3 self-mining to the 1.5 BTC/day run-rate, either of which would put the July-quarter collapse inside a document the market has not seen.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component checks out against primary documents -- I verified the 2026-04-15 POSASR (Post-Effective Amendment No. 1 to Reg. No. 333-285125, $270,000,000 on the fee table, with the explanatory note that 'the Registrant expects that it will cease to be a well-known seasoned issuer ... upon filing its Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025'), the 2026-06-15 exhibits-only auditor-consent POSAM No. 5, the Q1 cash walk of $80.8m to $43.5m, the $22.9m Q1 gross loss and the $21.1m short-term debt, and the complete absence of any 424B5 in 2026 after 2025-03-07, 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-04. This is the cleanest finding in the brief on facts. It is also the least published: the $270m shelf appears only as an automated filing summary on StockTitan (2026-04-28), framed there as 'a routine capital-raising mechanism', and the WKSI-loss motive and the shelf-to-market-cap ratio (~$270m against ~$249m of ADSs at $0.36) appear nowhere I could find. Against that: the balance-sheet stress itself is thoroughly priced -- the Q1 release carrying the cash collapse and the gross loss printed -13.66% on 2026-05-19, the largest move in the baseline and, notably, the one row in that untrustworthy history that IS a real earnings reaction. And the claim materially understates the mitigant: Canaan told the market on 2026-08-04 that it holds ~US$130m of digital assets and that 'our operations continue to generate bitcoin, providing us with a flexible source of capital', which is the company pre-announcing that it will sell BTC rather than hit the shelf. Dry powder plus motive is not a catalyst; the catalyst would be a takedown, and there has not been one in ten months at prices far above today's.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Automated filing summary noting Canaan registered $270,000,000 of securities on a post-effective amendment to its Form F-3, described as a routine capital-raising mechanism.
Q1 2026 release: revenue $62.7m, gross loss $22.9m, net loss $88.7m, cash $43.5m vs $80.8m at year-end 2025, short-term debt $21.1m, 690,594,191 ADSs outstanding.
Company states it holds ~US$130m of digital assets and will monetise a portion of the treasury to fund buybacks -- i.e. the stated funding path is BTC sales, not the shelf.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2026-05-19 Q1 print, which is where the cash burn became public, was -13.66% -- the largest reaction in the baseline and the only one I can confirm is a genuine earnings date. That move is the market pricing this balance sheet. No usable option chain means I cannot test whether downside is bid; put/call open interest of 0.03 on 6,882 contracts is too thin to read.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Q2 cash figure materially below ~$30m alongside a BTC count that has already been drawn down would convert this from capacity-and-motive into a live funding problem; conversely a Q2 cash balance stabilised by BTC sales kills it.
verdicts.factual_note: No error found. One nuance: POSAM No. 5 (2026-06-15) amends the same Reg. No. 333-285125 as the April POSASR, so the 'converted its automatic shelf' and the 'exhibits-only' filings are two amendments to one 2025 F-3ASR rather than a new registration.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The premise is factually false and that is the whole verdict. This cluster is not 'essentially invisible' -- Canaan issued a dedicated press release about it on PR Newswire on 2026-06-24 headlined 'Canaan Inc. Announces Open Market Share Purchases by Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer', disclosing that 'Zhang and Cheng together acquired a total of 1,065,000 American Depositary Shares of the Company at an average price of US$0.35 per ADS', with CEO commentary about conviction in the strategy. It was carried by Morningstar and written up by TipRanks ('Canaan Executives Buy Over 1 Million ADSs in Open-Market Purchases'). The stock fell 5.87% on the day of that release. Worse for the claim, the enumeration is incomplete: the three transactions listed total 565,000 ADSs, but Form 4 accession 0001802993-26-000003 (filed 2026-06-17) shows Zhang also bought 250,000 at $0.35 on 15 June and 250,000 at $0.35 on 16 June, so the real cluster is 1,065,000 ADSs -- exactly what the company said. The residual -- no insider filings since 22 June, no sales into the rally -- is an absence of EDGAR entries anyone can see in thirty seconds, and in dollars the whole cluster is ~$373k against a ~$249m market cap, 0.15%. Signal value only, and the signal was broadcast.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Company press release announcing the CEO and CFO together bought 1,065,000 ADSs in the open market at an average US$0.35.
The 6-K exhibit itself: 'Zhang and Cheng together acquired a total of 1,065,000 American Depositary Shares ("ADSs") of the Company at an average price of US$ 0.35 per ADS.'
Third-party writeup of the same purchases.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline's 2026-06-24 row is -5.87%. That is the date the insider buying was announced to the wire, and the market went down on it. A bullish reading of information the market already had and sold is agreement with a stale bid, not an edge.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A new Form 4 dated after 2026-08-17 -- insider buying with the Q2 numbers already in hand, rather than in June -- would be a different and genuinely unpublished finding.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The compliance facts are in the wire copy verbatim. Canaan press-released the second 180-day extension to 11 January 2027 on PR Newswire on 2026-07-15, including the exact sentence the hunter quotes about evaluating 'all available options during the second compliance period', and it was covered by Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, Blockspace and StockTitan the same day. The claim's own quotation of the company language is the tell: it is quoting a public press release. What is left is mechanism commentary -- that an ADS-ratio change needs no shareholder vote and can be effected in weeks, and that no depositary notice has appeared -- which is true, structural, and known to anyone who has watched a sub-$1 ADS before. Age is not novelty here: Canaan has been non-compliant through an entire first 180-day period. Crucially it does not reach this print. Nothing in a 30-June results release resolves a January 2027 bid-price deadline, the deadline is four months out, and the market's reaction on the day the extension was granted was +0.69% -- a shrug, because an extension is the benign outcome.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Company press release announcing the additional 180-day period to 11 January 2027 and the ten-consecutive-day $1.00 test.
Yahoo Finance wire item: 'Canaan gets 180-day Nasdaq extension to regain $1 bid price'.
Trade-press coverage of the same extension.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: +0.69% on 2026-07-15, the day the compliance notice was released. Spot at $0.36 is 111.8% above the 52-week low and the market is plainly aware the ADSs are far below $1.00 -- there is nothing latent about a price it can see.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A depositary notice or an EGM circular proposing an ADS-ratio change or reverse split, or the Q2 release itself announcing one, would move this to near-zero priced.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The lock-up was disclosed by Canaan itself in the deal announcement seven months ago and every number in the claim has been in print since February. Canaan's 2026-02-24 press release states the consideration was 'the issuance of 806,439,900 Canaan Inc. Class A ordinary shares to Cipher, equivalent to 53,762,660 American Depositary Shares ("ADS"), priced at US$0.7394 per ADS and subject to a lock-up period of six months' -- the ADS count, the price and the six-month term, all of it -- and it was carried by CoinDesk, The Block, Nasdaq, PR Newswire, Blockspace and DCD. Cipher's own 10-Q, which the hunter cites, restates the lock-up and its expiry, and Cipher's Q1 10-Q filed in May carried the same disclosure. More decisively, the event has already happened: the lock-up expired 2026-08-23 and the stock rose through it, +16% on 2026-08-25 into Bitcoin Asia, on ~23.5m ADS a day. Two full weeks of free-float have already traded post-expiry. And a lock-up expiry is not a thing a results release discloses or changes -- the mechanism has no route into the 8 September print at all.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Canaan's own release: 806,439,900 Class A shares / 53,762,660 ADS at US$0.7394 per ADS to Cipher, subject to a six-month lock-up.
The Block covers the ~$40m all-stock deal for Cipher's 49% of the West Texas (ABC) projects.
CoinDesk coverage of the same stock-funded acquisition.
Cipher's Q2 10-Q: 806,439,900 Canaan shares received, six-month lock-up commencing 19 February 2026 and expiring 23 August 2026, carried at $34.5m within prepaid expenses and other current assets.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 20-day window spans the 2026-08-23 expiry and the stock is +68.2% over it, including +16% on 2026-08-25. If a 7.8%-of-ADS unregistered block coming free were being priced, that is not the tape you would see. 53.76m ADS is ~2.3 days of the 23.45m 20-day average volume in a name running 183% annualised vol -- absorbable.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Schedule 13G/A or Cipher 8-K showing the block actually sold, or evidence Cipher was granted registration rights it has now exercised, would make this a live flow event rather than a resolved one.
verdicts.factual_note: Two corrections. The percentage is overstated: 53,762,660 against the 690,594,191 ADSs Canaan reported outstanding at 31 March 2026 is 7.8%, not 9.2%; the '585.8m float' is a data-provider figure, not a company number. And Cipher's 10-Q dates the lock-up as commencing 19 February 2026 (shares received that date), not 23 February, though the 23 August expiry is as stated.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The 'no new authorisation' point is in the plain text of the release it debunks. The 2026-08-04 exhibit says repurchases will occur 'under the Company's existing share repurchase authorization' effective 12 December 2025, gives no dollar figure, and PR Newswire and Globe-and-Mail coverage of it said the same -- the announcement 'did not authorize a new repurchase amount'. The execution history is public too: the Q1 release of 2026-05-19 disclosed ~2.8m ADSs for ~US$2.0m under the current programme, and the 2025-12-17 6-K disclosed that the prior US$30m programme from 27 May 2025 had bought 6,586,413 ADSs for ~US$4.9m, which MarketScreener and Investing.com both wrote up. So the arithmetic the claim performs (6.7% and 16% execution) is arithmetic on published figures, not a discovery. The causal framing is also wrong in a way that damages the thesis: the 2026-08-04 release produced +12.43% on the day and then faded -- spot was ~$0.214 around 2026-08-06 and only $0.2712 on 2026-08-20 -- and the +68% run was lit by the CLARITY Act push on 2026-08-20 (+12.95%) and Bitcoin Asia on 2026-08-25 (+16%), not by the buyback release. There is therefore little buyback premium left to deflate. Finally the claim's own catalyst is self-defeating: repurchases 'through 30 June' predate the 4 August announcement entirely, so the Q2 number can barely differ from the $2.0m already disclosed on 19 May and tells you nothing about whether the BTC-funded buying has actually happened. What is genuinely unpriced is thin: that a US$30m authorisation is 12% of market cap and this management has executed 6.7% of it, which is a credibility point rather than a numbers point.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The release states repurchases will be made under the existing board authorisation effective 12 December 2025, subject to Board oversight and to the limits of that authorisation, with no new dollar amount.
Q1 release discloses the US$30m authorisation and ~2.8m ADSs repurchased for ~US$2.0m under it.
Discloses that the prior US$30m programme beginning 27 May 2025 repurchased 6,586,413 ADSs for ~US$4.9m, and announces the new US$30m programme from 12 December 2025.
Third-party coverage of the renewal, including the prior programme's US$4.9m of execution.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: +12.43% on 2026-08-04, then a fade: the 20-day run-up of 68.2% measures from ~$0.214 on 2026-08-06, i.e. below where the release left the stock, and the subsequent gains are dated to 2026-08-20 (CLARITY Act, +12.95% to $0.2712) and 2026-08-25 (+16%, Bitcoin Asia). The buyback pop is already gone from the tape. The last 5 days are -5.26%.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the Q2 release discloses repurchases through the release date rather than through 30 June and the figure is still near $2m, the claim becomes a genuine same-day disappointment; if it shows meaningful August BTC-funded buying it inverts.

interactions: The factual disagreement I was asked to resolve does not exist, and the documents are unambiguous. CAN-a#1 asserts zero 424B5 takedowns anywhere in 2026 and that is exactly right: EDGAR shows Canaan's 424B5 filings ending at 2025-11-04 (the US$72m Brevan Howard / Galaxy / Weiss registered direct at US$1.131 per ADS), with 2025-10-24 and 2025-03-07 before it and nothing since (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001780652&type=424). So there has been no ATM and no registered takedown in 2026. The one large 2026 issuance is unregistered and is the subject of CAN-b#0: 806,439,900 Class A shares / 53,762,660 ADS issued to Cipher in February 2026 as deal consideration. That is precisely why CAN-b#0's Rule 144 point works -- the shares were never registered for resale. A share-count reconciliation that saw ADSs outstanding rise into the 690,594,191 reported at 31 March 2026 and inferred shelf issuance would be reading the Cipher private placement as an ATM. Both hunters are consistent with the filings; neither is wrong on this. Three other interactions. (1) CAN-a#2 and CAN-b#0 are mirrors on the same float -- insiders bought 1,065,000 ADSs at $0.33-0.35 in June while Cipher holds 53,762,660 ADSs marked at $0.7394 and now worth ~$19m; the insider buying is 2% of the Cipher block, so as a supply-demand argument the bullish claim is fifty times smaller than the bearish one and neither is unpublished. (2) CAN-a#1 and CAN-b#1 point opposite ways off the same balance sheet: one says the company is cash-constrained and keeping a shelf equal to its market cap alive, the other says it announced it would sell bitcoin to buy back stock. Both can be true simultaneously (monetise BTC instead of issuing equity), but they cannot both be the story the print tells, and the 2026-08-04 release explicitly chooses the BTC path -- which is a mitigant CAN-a#1 does not price. (3) CAN-a#0's July release (2026-08-17) and CAN-b#1's buyback release (2026-08-04) sit in the same 6-K stream two weeks apart and both are inside the 20-day window, so any run-up attribution has to allocate between them and the two macro days that actually explain it. Finally, on the baseline: I did not use the eight-row reaction history as a base rate, but one of its rows is real -- 2026-05-19 was the Q1 2026 results 6-K and printed -13.66%. That is the only defensible earnings-reaction anchor for this name, and it is roughly triple the baseline's 4.5% expected move. Note also that management guided Q2 revenue to US$35-45m against Q1's US$62.7m, so the revenue decline itself is pre-guided and none of these six findings is about beating or missing that guide.
